The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse are biblical figures from the Book of Revelation who symbolize destructive end-time forces. As the first four of the seven seals are opened, four riders emerge on distinctively colored horses: Conquest (White), War (Red), Famine (Black), and Death (Pale). [1, 2]

The four horses represent distinct calamities: [1]

White Horse (Conquest): Ridden by a conqueror wearing a crown and carrying a bow. Interpretations of this figure range from representing military conquest and the Antichrist to Jesus Christ. [1, 2]

Red Horse (War): Ridden by a figure carrying a large sword, symbolizing bloodshed, violence, and the end of peace on earth. [1]

Black Horse (Famine): The rider carries a pair of balance scales, representing economic scarcity and famine, where basic food staples become exorbitantly expensive. [1, 2]

Pale Horse (Death): The only rider explicitly named is Death, followed closely by Hades. The horse is often described as pale green, symbolizing sickness and pestilence. [1, 2, 3]
